title: Daily air quality index by county
description: The daily Air Quality Index (AQI) for every US county with an EPA monitor, from 1980 to yesterday. Rows up to EPA's latest AirData release are validated (validated: true). Later days are preliminary (validated: false): EPA AirNow data from federal, state, local and tribal agencies, not yet verified and subject to change. For those days the county AQI is a derived value calculated by airdata.dev as the highest site AQI reported to AirNow in the county that day, the way EPA summarizes a county; the site AQI values themselves are as received. Preliminary days cover ozone, PM2.5, PM10 and CO only. A preliminary row never replaces a validated one.

source.name: EPA AirData daily AQI by county (validated) and EPA AirNow daily data files (preliminary)
source.publisher: US EPA (AirData, AirNow) and the AirNow partner agencies
source.attribution: Validated data: US Environmental Protection Agency. Air Quality System Data Mart [internet database] available via https://www.epa.gov/outdoor-air-quality-data. Accessed on this version's retrieval date. Preliminary data (validated: false): courtesy of the federal, state, local and tribal air quality agencies that own the data (https://www.airnow.gov/partners/) and the EPA AirNow program. These data are preliminary: not fully verified or validated, and subject to change. Preliminary county AQI values are derived by airdata.dev as the highest site AQI in the county; site values are as received from AirNow.

title: Current orbital elements
description: The newest general perturbations (SGP4) element set for every object in Earth orbit that the US Space Force publishes, as CCSDS Orbit Mean-Elements Message fields, with period, semi-major axis, perigee and apogee derived from them. Catalog numbers are full integers, so objects numbered 100000 and up are included.

source.name: Space-Track.org GP class (current general perturbations element sets)
source.attribution: Orbital data from Space-Track.org, provided by USSPACECOM (18th Space Defense Squadron).

schema.name: norad_cat_id
schema.description: US Space Force catalog number (up to nine digits)

schema.name: norad_block
schema.description: norad_cat_id rounded down to a multiple of 1000: the partition file holding the object

schema.name: object_name
schema.description: OBJECT_NAME

schema.name: object_id
schema.description: OBJECT_ID: international designator (2025-001A), or UNKNOWN

schema.name: epoch
schema.description: EPOCH of the mean elements, UTC

schema.name: mean_motion
schema.description: Kozai mean motion (SGP4)

schema.name: ra_of_asc_node
schema.description: Right ascension of the ascending node

schema.name: bstar
schema.description: SGP4 drag term

schema.name: classification_type
schema.description: U for unclassified

schema.name: period_min
schema.description: 1440 / mean_motion

schema.name: semimajor_axis_km
schema.description: From mean motion by Kepler's third law with SGP4's WGS-72 constants (mu 398600.8 km^3/s^2); approximate

schema.name: perigee_km
schema.description: semimajor_axis_km * (1 - e) minus the WGS-72 equatorial radius (6378.135 km); approximate

schema.name: apogee_km
schema.description: semimajor_axis_km * (1 + e) minus 6378.135 km; approximate

schema.name: center_name
schema.description: CENTER_NAME (EARTH)

schema.name: ref_frame
schema.description: REF_FRAME (TEME)

schema.name: time_system
schema.description: TIME_SYSTEM (UTC)

schema.name: mean_element_theory
schema.description: MEAN_ELEMENT_THEORY (SGP4)

schema.name: originator
schema.description: ORIGINATOR of the message

schema.name: creation_date
schema.description: When Space-Track generated the message (UTC)

title: Launch log
description: Every launch in GCAT's launch list, one row per launch since 1942: orbital and deep-space launches with their international designation, plus missiles, sounding rockets and other suborbital flights. Each row has the date and time at the precision GCAT knows it, the vehicle, launch site, agency and outcome.

source.name: General Catalog of Artificial Space Objects (GCAT), launch list
source.attribution: data from GCAT (J. McDowell, planet4589.org/space/gcat)

schema.name: launch_tag
schema.description: COSPAR designation for orbital launches (1998-067; Harvard style before 1963, 1957 ALP), GCAT's own yyyy-Xnnn tag for others (1942-A01, 1957-F01 failed orbital)

schema.name: launch_class
schema.description: LaunchCode category: orbital, deep-space, missile, lofted-missile, near-orbital, test-rocket, atmospheric, suborbital, high-altitude-sounding, reentry-test, off-earth (from another world), crewed-suborbital, not-a-launch (GCAT placeholder entries)

schema.name: launch_date
schema.description: UTC date of first motion; null when GCAT knows it less precisely than a day, or gives a day after its own file date (a typo, e.g. 2026-M02 dated 2027 Jan 3); see launch_date_text

schema.name: launch_time
schema.description: UTC time at exactly the precision GCAT gives (to the minute, second or millisecond); null when it is less precise or uncertain

schema.name: launch_date_text
schema.description: The date exactly as GCAT writes it, in its Vague Date format ('1957 Oct  4 1928:34', '1944 Jan', '1971?')

schema.name: launch_date_precision
schema.description: Precision of launch_date_text: millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, month, quarter, year, ...; '(uncertain)' when it ends in ?, which widens it by one unit each way. Null if GCAT's text is not a valid vague date

schema.name: launch_jd
schema.description: GCAT's Julian Date (UTC) of launch, for sorting; nominal when the date is vague

schema.name: lv_type
schema.description: Launch vehicle type

schema.name: flight_id
schema.description: Serial number or mission number of this flight

schema.name: platform
schema.description: Mobile launch platform (ship, submarine, aircraft), if any

schema.name: launch_site
schema.description: GCAT launch site code

schema.name: ascent_site
schema.description: Where the rocket actually ignited, when different (air launches: the drop zone)

schema.name: apogee_km
schema.description: Highest altitude of a suborbital flight, or apogee of the initial orbit

schema.name: apogee_estimated
schema.description: GCAT marks the apogee with ? (a guess from the vehicle's capability)

schema.name: orbital_payload_t
schema.description: Payload mass delivered to orbit (0 when nothing reached orbit); GCAT generates it from its payload tables and asks users to treat it with caution

schema.name: agency
schema.description: GCAT org code of the launch service provider

schema.name: launch_code
schema.description: GCAT LaunchCode: category letter plus outcome (OS, OF, MS, OS80, ...)

schema.name: outcome
schema.description: success (propulsive success; the payload may still have failed), failure, unknown, pad-explosion or pad-abort. Null for not-a-launch entries

schema.name: success_percent
schema.description: GCAT's partial-success score for reliability statistics (OS80 -> 80); null for plain S or F

schema.name: category
schema.description: For orbital launches GCAT's launch profile code (Sat LEO O); for others the kind of flight (Meteo, Aeron, Test, Weapon)

title: Satellite catalog
description: Every artificial object GCAT catalogs, one record per object since Sputnik in 1957: payloads, rocket stages, components and debris, including those that reentered, left for deep space or failed to reach orbit. Each record has the GCAT id, the US catalog number (six digits and up since the 2026 rollover), the international designator, owner, state, launch and decay dates, mass, status and the latest orbit with its class.

source.name: General Catalog of Artificial Space Objects (GCAT), object catalogs and currentcat
source.attribution: data from GCAT (J. McDowell, planet4589.org/space/gcat)

schema.name: jcat
schema.description: GCAT's object id: catalog letter (S, A, T, F) and sequence number, e.g. S25544

schema.name: norad_cat_id
schema.description: US Space Force (NORAD) catalog number. Not unique: objects that stayed attached share their parent's number, and the S-catalog row (jcat S plus the number) is the one the US catalog lists. Null when GCAT does not tie the object to a number (see satcat_note), including S entries it cannot match to a specific satellite of the launch

schema.name: satcat_note
schema.description: GCAT's reason for a missing catalog number: NNA (not assigned or not identified), NNA A/C/E/I/P/R/S/T/X (attached, component, spacesuit, internal, partial orbit, ...), NSO (suborbital)

schema.name: piece
schema.description: International (COSPAR) designator as GCAT records it, e.g. 1998-067A. Launches before 1963 keep their original Harvard designations (1957 ALP 2), which Space-Track shows renumbered (1957-001B)

schema.name: launch_tag
schema.description: Launch the object belongs to; joins launches.launch_tag

schema.name: catalog
schema.description: GCAT catalog holding the object: satcat, satcat100k, satcat270k, auxcat, tmpcat or ftocat

schema.name: name
schema.description: GCAT's recommended current name (after any renaming)

schema.name: original_name
schema.description: Name in the object's first phase

schema.name: object_type
schema.description: payload, rocket-stage, component, debris, suborbital-payload or spurious (GCAT SatType byte 1)

schema.name: gcat_type
schema.description: GCAT's 12-byte SatType string (byte 1 coarse type, byte 2 modifier, byte 3 attachment, byte 4 subtype, ...)

schema.name: identity_uncertain
schema.description: SatType byte 9 is '?': GCAT knows the objects of the launch but not which catalog number is which

schema.name: status_group
schema.description: in-orbit, lost (in orbit but untracked), reentered (decayed, deorbited or landed), suborbital, deep-space, failed-to-orbit, broken-up (exploded or destroyed in a collision) or spurious (no real object)

schema.name: status_code
schema.description: GCAT phase status code of the latest phase: O in orbit, AO attached in orbit, OX lost, R reentered, D deorbited, L landed, AR reentered attached, DSO deep space, E exploded, ERR not a real object, ... A trailing ? marks it unconfirmed

schema.name: status
schema.description: GCAT's plain-language current status (currentcat ExpandedStatus), e.g. 'Attached to S25544 Zarya'. Null for objects currentcat does not cover (ftocat and a few others)

schema.name: active
schema.description: GCAT counts the object as an active satellite (currentcat Ac = A). Null where currentcat does not cover it

schema.name: owner
schema.description: GCAT org code of the owner/operator in the latest phase (e.g. SPXS, JSC). A trailing ? marks an uncertain attribution; joint owners are slash-separated

schema.name: owner_name
schema.description: Owner's name from GCAT's organizations table

schema.name: state
schema.description: GCAT code of the country or intergovernmental body responsible (US, CN, SU, F for France, I-ESA, ...); not ISO codes

schema.name: launch_date
schema.description: UTC launch date; null when GCAT gives it only roughly, or gives a day after its own file date (a typo); see launch_date_text

schema.name: launch_date_text
schema.description: Launch date exactly as GCAT writes it, in its Vague Date format ('1957 Oct  4', '1971?')

schema.name: decay_date
schema.description: UTC date the object reentered, landed, crashed or impacted another body; null while in orbit or flying, and when GCAT gives the date only roughly

schema.name: decay_date_text
schema.description: That date exactly as GCAT writes it ('1958 Jan  4?', '1960 Apr 26 1730?')

schema.name: mass_kg
schema.description: Mass at orbital insertion, not counting attached objects. Null when GCAT gives none (0 or '-'), as for most debris

schema.name: mass_estimated
schema.description: GCAT flags the mass as an estimate (good to about 20%)

schema.name: orbit_source
schema.description: latest: currentcat's most recent orbit (objects still in space); canonical: the representative early-operations orbit GCAT lists for the latest phase

schema.name: orbit_epoch
schema.description: Epoch of that orbit when GCAT pins it to a day

schema.name: period_min
schema.description: Orbital period (latest orbits only)

schema.name: perigee_km
schema.description: Perigee height above the central body's equatorial radius. Negative for trajectories that intersect the Earth or are hyperbolic

schema.name: apogee_km
schema.description: Apogee height. Negative for hyperbolic (escape) trajectories; null where GCAT writes Inf

schema.name: inclination_deg
schema.description: Inclination to the equator of date (Earth orbits)

schema.name: orbit_estimated
schema.description: GCAT flags a perigee/apogee/inclination value as a guess

schema.name: orbit_category
schema.description: GCAT OpOrbit category: LLEO/I, LEO/S, MEO, HEO/M, GTO, GEO/S, GEO/ID, VHEO, CLO, EEO, ...

schema.name: orbit_class
schema.description: LEO (below 2000 km), MEO, GEO (geosynchronous, incl. inclined and drifting), HEO (highly elliptical incl. Molniya and GTO), VHEO, cislunar, escape or suborbital, mapped from orbit_category

title: Daily streamflow
description: Daily mean discharge at every USGS stream gage over the last 400 days, flagged provisional, estimated or ice-affected, with the USGS qualifier codes. Re-read in full every day, because USGS revises provisional values for months.

source.attribution: Streamflow data courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey.

title: Active fires (US and Canada)
description: Satellite fire detections from the last 7 days over the United States and Canada, grouped into fire events and linked to the official incident (name, acres, containment, IRWIN id) where one exists. Detections in the same or adjacent 1 km grid cells within 48 hours of each other form one event; repeat views of the same spot by a second satellite on the same overpass are counted once. Built from NASA FIRMS VIIRS near-real-time detections (S-NPP, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21), NIFC WFIGS current incidents and perimeters, and Natural Earth state and province boundaries.

source.name: NASA LANCE FIRMS VIIRS 375 m Active Fire NRT (VNP14IMGTDL_NRT, VJ114IMGTDL_NRT, VJ214IMGTDL_NRT); incidents and perimeters from NIFC WFIGS; boundaries from Natural Earth
source.attribution: We acknowledge the use of imagery from the NASA LANCE FIRMS (https://earthdata.nasa.gov/firms), part of the NASA Earth Science Data and Information System (ESDIS). VIIRS 375 m active fire NRT products: S-NPP doi:10.5067/FIRMS/VIIRS/VNP14IMGT_NRT.002, NOAA-20 doi:10.5067/FIRMS/VIIRS/VJ114IMGT_NRT.002, NOAA-21 doi:10.5067/FIRMS/VIIRS/VJ214IMGT_NRT.002. Incident data: National Interagency Fire Center, Wildland Fire Interagency Geospatial Services (WFIGS). Boundaries: Made with Natural Earth.
